Portland at a glance

Portland is Maine's largest city, built on a peninsula in Casco Bay. It borders South Portland, Westbrook and Falmouth, with about 21 square miles of land inside a much larger water boundary. The July 2025 estimate is 69,911 residents.

The peninsula and the mainland neighborhoods act like separate markets. The Old Port, Bayside, the Arts District, Munjoy Hill and the West End sit on or near the peninsula, and Deering covers the northern and eastern sections. Peaks, Great Diamond, Little Diamond, Cushing and Cliff islands belong to the city as well, with year-round ferry service from Casco Bay Lines.

Age and construction differ a lot between those areas. Portland burned badly in 1866, and buyers still ask about the age of peninsula buildings because of it. Deering was annexed in 1899 and has a different mix of housing, so comparable sales matter more than any citywide figure.

  • Ask for a full inspection history, since older masonry and wood-frame buildings can hide different problems.
  • Island properties carry ferry and utility questions a buyer will raise.
  • A short walk to a bus line or to the peninsula is worth a line in any listing, since it widens the pool of buyers who prefer not to drive daily.

Flood and weather questions

Portland's ocean-moderated climate still brings snow, wind-driven rain and tidal flooding. Water is the longer-term concern: the 2024 record high tide reached 14.57 feet, and sea level is projected to rise roughly six inches by 2050 and two feet by 2060. A house near the waterfront, on a low street or on an island should expect flood zone and insurance questions from buyers and their lenders.

  • Check the FEMA flood map for your parcel before listing.
  • Ask your insurance agent for a flood quote so you can answer buyers.
  • Document sump pumps, drainage work and any past water in the basement.

How does Portland property tax work after the revaluation?

The 2025 revaluation raised values sharply and lowered the mil rate, so what you owe depends on how your own value moved. The city has about 19,400 residential properties and 1,920 commercial ones, with taxable real estate near $19.7 billion. After the 2021 revaluation the City Council voted to reassess every five years. Revaluations bring assessed values in line with the current market, as state law requires, and they shift the burden by value rather than raising total revenue.

Portland before and after the 2025 revaluation
MeasureBeforeFiscal 2026
Mil rate per $1,000$15.01$11.98
Median residential value$396,700$566,600

That is a 43 percent jump in the median residential value. Taxes are paid in two halves, one in the fall and one in March. The city's tax page shows the current year's dates. Maine's lien timeline runs from the commitment date, so a balance left open for months gets harder to deal with.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Portland house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What if you owe property tax on a Portland house?

You can still sell with tax unpaid, because the payoff comes out of your proceeds at closing. Start by asking the city for a current balance, then give it to the title company so the closing statement shows it. Maine sets the lien steps in 36 M.R.S. section 942 and section 943. A demand notice can go out between 8 months and a year after commitment, and a lien that gets recorded ranks as a mortgage ahead of the others.

When tax, interest and costs stay unpaid for 18 months after filing, the lien is treated as foreclosed. The owner and any mortgage holders must be told 30 to 45 days before that date.

  • An application to fix an error or illegality in an assessment is due within 185 days of commitment, under section 841.
  • A hardship abatement on a primary residence can be requested within 3 years of commitment.
  • A seller who paid a pro rata share under a written proration agreement can ask the treasurer to record a certificate that says so.

Transfer tax and recording costs

Expect a transfer tax of $2.20 per $500 of value, with the buyer and the seller each paying half. From November 1, 2025, any transfer also owes $3.80 per $500 on the portion over $1 million, which makes early math worthwhile for owners of pricier peninsula homes.

Filing the deed costs $40 for most submitters, and a claimed exemption has to be written on the declaration of value form. Ask the title company to put these figures, along with your payoff and any unpaid tax, on a draft settlement statement a few days before you sign.

What to expect between offer and closing

Once you accept an offer, the title company searches the record for liens, confirms who owns the house and prepares a settlement statement. Your tax balance, mortgage payoff and half of the transfer tax come out of the price. The deed is recorded after closing.

Sellers who have the paperwork ready move fastest. Bring the deed, the mortgage statement, any lien notices and, for a rental, the tenant list with lease dates and your registration status. For a house near the water or on an island, have the flood map and insurance quote ready for the buyer's lender.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Portland houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Rental registration rules for Portland owners

Residential rental units in Portland are registered every year, and short-term rentals carry a separate registration. The deadline is December 31, or thirty days after you start renting. Under Chapter 6 of the city code, a new owner or manager applies within 30 days of buying.

Both buyers and sellers feel this rule. Own a building with tenants? Check that your registration is current before listing, since a buyer's attorney will ask. Used the house for short-term rentals? Each listing needs your registration number, and registration allows on-site inspections. The city also has a Housing Safety and Rent Control office, and its code includes tenant protections.

A cash sale of a tenant-occupied house means you need not empty the building first, though Maine notice rules and lease terms still apply.

How can I sell a Portland house quickly?

Cash is the quickest way to close, while a listing can net more for a house in good shape. Portland's buyer demand helps a listing, but you still prepare the house, host showings and wait out a financing contingency. A cash buyer skips the repair requests and the appraisal.

  • Gather the deed, your mortgage payoff and any lien notices.
  • For a rental, note tenants, lease end dates and registration status.
  • Set the offer beside a listing's likely net after repairs, commission and months of holding costs.

Our written offers cover Portland houses in any condition, with no commission or fees to you. If the numbers do not work, you can walk away.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Portland, Maine mil rate?

For fiscal 2026 it is $11.98 per $1,000 of assessed value, down from $15.01, after the city's revaluation. Check the City of Portland tax page for the current year.

When are Portland property taxes due?

Each year's bill is paid in two halves, one in the fall and one in March. Confirm the exact days with the city before choosing a closing date.

Can I sell a Portland house with a tax lien?

Yes. Closing proceeds pay the tax, interest and lien costs. Once 18 months pass after filing without redemption, a recorded lien is treated as foreclosed.

Who pays Maine transfer tax in Portland?

They split it evenly at $2.20 per $500 of value. Transfers from November 1, 2025 add $3.80 per $500 above $1 million.

Do I need to register a rental before selling in Portland?

Yes, registration is annual, due by December 31 or thirty days after renting begins. New owners apply within 30 days of buying, so a current registration smooths the sale.

Lewiston at a glance

Find Lewiston on the Androscoggin River's east bank in Androscoggin County, about midway between Augusta and Portland. Across the water is Auburn, its twin. Roughly 34 of the city's 35.5 square miles are land, and Maine Turnpike access suits buyers who commute out of town.

The 2020 census recorded 37,121 people living in 16,579 housing units, 7.8 percent of them empty. Growth since then has been slow, with 38,866 residents estimated in July 2025.

Textile-mill wealth built most of the older stock: multi-family blocks, three-deckers and small wood-frame houses on narrow lots, many a hundred years old or more. Owners of those should plan for buyer questions on the roof, knob-and-tube wiring, heating and lead paint, with repair quotes pulling the price down.

  • Older wood-frame houses near downtown often have mixed upgrades from different decades.
  • Buildings with three or more units have to register as rentals, as covered below.
  • Condition varies block by block, so a street-level view matters more than a citywide average.

What a Maine winter does to a Lewiston house

The heating system and the roof take the load here. After a hard season, inspectors and buyers check a short list:

  • Ice dams at roof edges, plus attic insulation and ventilation.
  • Oil tank age and location, and whether the furnace or boiler has been serviced.
  • Frost damage to foundations, porch footings and chimneys.
  • Basement moisture, since the city sits beside a river and spring melt raises the water table.

Deferred work on any of these often stalls a regular sale once the inspection report arrives, and it pushes many owners toward an as-is cash buyer.

Lewiston property tax and the revaluation

With a mil rate above $30 and a revaluation underway, tax comes up in nearly every Lewiston sale. Rates below are per $1,000 of assessed value.

Lewiston mil rates by fiscal year
Fiscal yearMil rate per $1,000
2025$31.77
2026$32.78
2027$34.15

The last citywide revaluation took effect in 1988. The state found Lewiston's assessments too low compared with sales, so the city hired Tyler Technologies of Yarmouth to redo them. The new values reflect fair market value as of April 1, 2026, and they will be implemented for the 2027 tax year, which is fiscal 2028.

Your present bill rests on old values, so a buyer will weigh the new value too, not just the bill you hand over.

The assessing and treasury offices share the address 27 Pine Street. Assessor: 207-513-3122, open Monday, Wednesday and Thursday 7:45 AM to 4 PM and Tuesday 7:45 AM to 5:30 PM, closed Friday. Treasury: 207-513-3131, Monday to Friday 8:30 AM to 4 PM. Ask the Assessor what the new value will be for your parcel and bring that number to your first conversation with a buyer.

What happens if property tax goes unpaid?

Unpaid tax in Maine can end in an automatic foreclosure, but the timeline is slow enough that selling usually solves it. First comes a 30-day demand notice, which 36 M.R.S. section 942 allows the collector to send anywhere from 8 months to a year after commitment. If nothing is paid, a lien certificate gets recorded at the registry of deeds.

That recorded lien acts like a mortgage and outranks the others. Under section 943, a lien that sits 18 months without payment of tax, interest and costs is treated as foreclosed, and the owner loses the right to redeem. The treasurer has to warn the owner 30 to 45 days ahead.

  • A closing during the redemption period clears the lien out of your proceeds.
  • A seller who paid a pro rata share under a written proration agreement can have the treasurer record a certificate saying so.
  • A primary residence may qualify for hardship abatement under 36 M.R.S. section 841(2), and a written decision is due within 30 days.

If you believe a value is wrong or illegal, a written abatement request is due within 185 days of commitment. Do not sit on it.

Transfer taxes and recording fees

Each side pays half of Maine's transfer tax, which totals $2.20 for every $500 of value. On sales up to $1 million that means $1.10 per $500 apiece. A surcharge of $3.80 per $500 applies to the slice above $1 million on transfers from November 1, 2025 onward, which seldom touches a Lewiston house.

A deed costs $40 to record for most filers. File the deed with a transfer tax declaration at the county registry, naming any exemption you claim. Maine Revenue Services posts the rules.

At the closing table, the title company subtracts your mortgage payoff, any unpaid property tax and your half of the transfer tax from the price. Ask for a draft settlement statement a few days ahead so every figure is familiar before you sign, and bring the deed and a photo ID.

Do Lewiston landlords and sellers of rentals need to register?

Yes, once a building holds three or more units. An owner who lives in one of the units still has to register, while a two-unit building is left out. No fee is charged. Skipping registration risks civil penalties and makes the building ineligible for city loans or grants.

A new multi-family building registers within 30 days after its certificate of occupancy. The City Clerk, at 207-513-3124, can confirm current wording.

Planning and Code Enforcement, 207-513-3125, applies the Maine Uniform Building and Energy Code, in force locally since September 28, 2011. Close out open permits and unfinished work before you list, since a buyer's attorney will look for them.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Lewiston houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Ways to sell a house fast in Lewiston

Three paths exist: list, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer. Time and price pull in opposite directions. A house in good order may net more on the market, but showings, inspection negotiation and a buyer's mortgage stretch the timeline. A sale by owner skips the commission and leaves marketing and contracts to you.

With a cash buyer such as us, repairs and financing drop out of the picture. We purchase as-is, which lets a Lewiston house with a worn roof, a tenant or a lien still close. Our offer will sit below a polished retail sale, so measure it against your net once repairs, commission and carrying costs come off.

  • Call the Treasury office first to learn what you owe.
  • Pull together the deed, a mortgage payoff and tenant details if any.
  • Get the offer in writing and see who covers each closing cost.

Any offer, ours included, is yours to refuse. Taking a week to compare two or three options costs little next to choosing the wrong one.

Frequently asked questions

How much is the Lewiston tax rate?

Fiscal 2027 sits at $34.15 per $1,000 of assessed value, after $32.78 in fiscal 2026 and $31.77 in fiscal 2025.

When do new Lewiston property values take effect?

They start with the 2027 tax year, which is fiscal 2028, and reflect fair market value as of April 1, 2026.

Can I sell a Lewiston house with unpaid property taxes?

Yes. Closing pays off the tax, interest and lien costs from your proceeds. A recorded lien that stays unpaid for 18 months is treated as foreclosed, so acting sooner leaves more choices.

Who pays the Maine transfer tax?

Both sides share it equally at $2.20 per $500 of value. Transfers from November 1, 2025 add $3.80 per $500 on the part above $1 million.

Do I have to register a Lewiston duplex as a rental?

No. The duty starts at three units. A call to the City Clerk will confirm current wording.

Selling in Bangor?

Bangor at a glance

Bangor is the seat and largest city of Penobscot County and the third most populous city in Maine, with 31,753 residents at the 2020 census. Only Portland and Lewiston are bigger. It sits on the Penobscot River, about 30 miles upstream from the Atlantic, and covers 34.59 square miles, of which 34.26 are land.

The city works as the shopping, health care and services hub for a five-county area of more than 330,000 people. Buyers can come from other towns in the region, from the university communities nearby and from hospital and service employers.

Much of the older housing near downtown was built after the fires that struck the city in the 1800s and the Great Fire of 1911, and the lumber-era mansions are still standing. Older homes bring older systems, so expect a buyer to ask about wiring, the roof and heating.

Winter and flood issues buyers ask about

Bangor has cold, snowy winters, and inspectors look hard at roof condition, insulation, heating fuel type and basement moisture. Owners of vacant houses also worry about frozen and burst pipes, so a house left empty through winter deserves a quick check.

The Penobscot River can flood from precipitation and snowmelt, and ice jams can cause sudden local flooding, mostly in spring. If your house is near the river or Kenduskeag Stream, look up FEMA's flood map for your address before you list, and be ready for insurance questions.

How are Bangor property taxes set and paid?

The Assessing Office values property, and the mill rate is set after the municipal, county and school budgets and the property values are final. The city hired KRT Appraisal to run a citywide revaluation that began in spring 2024, so assessed values may differ a great deal from what older tax bills showed. Call the Assessing Office to see how the revaluation changed your property.

The City Clerk and Treasury office handles tax bills. A council resolution from June 8, 2026 sets interest on overdue first-half payments at the maximum State-approved rate, 7.0 percent per year for 2026. Your current bill shows the exact due dates, and the Treasury office can confirm them.

When you sell, ask the closer to prorate the current tax period so you pay only for the days you owned the house.

Who to call

City Clerk and TreasuryTax bills and payments, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:15 p.m.207-992-4200

Vacant buildings, short-term rentals and rent notices

Bangor has three local rules worth knowing before a sale: vacant building registration, short-term rental regulation and the rent increase notice rule.

  • Vacant buildings. A registration is required within 60 days of a building becoming vacant, for buildings in listed zoning districts such as URD-1, URD-2, M&SD, NSD, DDD, LDR, HDR and RR&A. Primary residences of active-duty service members are exempt, and so are owners on extended absences who have a property manager and an emergency contact. The registration gives police, fire and code enforcement a contact for the owner.
  • Fee deferral. An owner whose primary residence became uninhabitable after a fire or other casualty, or who holds an active building permit, can ask to defer the fee for up to six months. The application goes to Code Enforcement.
  • Short-term rentals. The City Council adopted short-term rental regulations on October 23, 2023, including address-number visibility requirements.
  • Rent increases. A landlord of a residential unit in Bangor must give a tenant 60 days' written notice of a rent increase.

If you inherited an empty house or are moving out before a sale, ask Code Enforcement whether the 60-day clock has started.

What it costs to sell a house in Bangor

Your costs as seller: half the Maine transfer tax, whatever you still owe on the mortgage and in property tax, and recording charges. The tax is $2.20 per $500 of value and is shared by buyer and seller in equal parts. Our Maine transfer tax guide explains the exemptions that apply to inheritances, divorces and lender deeds.

A Penobscot County deed is recorded at the county registry of deeds, at a statutory fee of $35 plus a $5 surcharge at most registries. Our Maine deed recording guide explains the format and fees, and the registry can confirm its hours before you file.

Have these ready: the deed, a payoff letter, the current tax bill and, for a vacant or rented house, registration paperwork.

From offer to closing in Bangor

The sequence barely changes with the route you pick. Buyer and seller sign a purchase agreement, a title search shows who owns the house and what encumbers it, and the closer drafts a statement of figures. After signing, the deed goes to the registry for recording, and your mortgage and any tax balance are settled from the money due to you.

  • Prorate the current tax period, so each side covers only its own days.
  • Clear the mortgage balance and unpaid property tax out of the proceeds.
  • Share the Maine transfer tax evenly with the buyer.
  • Keep a copy of the recorded deed.

Selling for cash avoids the appraisal and lender conditions, where financed deals often stall. Title work stays, though, so back taxes, liens and an absent heir's signature all need solving first.

Tenants keep their rights through a sale. If you plan a rent increase before selling, you still owe 60 days' written notice, and buyers will want to see the leases.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Bangor houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Should you list, sell yourself or take a cash offer?

Listing gets the most buyers through the door but demands the most prep. Selling by owner keeps the commission and leaves showings and paperwork to you. With a cash offer there is no mortgage contingency, the buyer typically takes the house as-is, and you choose the closing date.

We buy as-is in Bangor: houses needing repairs, inherited homes, rentals with tenants and properties with mortgage arrears. We quote no prices in advance. We review the property and make an offer, and you can turn it down without owing us anything. A cash offer is often lower than a retail listing, so add up repairs, carrying costs, commission and time before you compare.

Cash tends to work best when a house sits empty through a Maine winter, when a vacant building registration is looming, or when an estate wants a firm closing date. Whatever you decide, check with Code Enforcement first on any vacant building registration, and keep the current tax bill and deed handy for the title company.

Frequently asked questions

How do I sell my house fast in Bangor, ME?

A cash sale to a buyer who purchases as-is is usually the quickest route, since there is no mortgage approval or appraisal. Listing with an agent can take longer because financed buyers order inspections.

How many people live in Bangor, Maine?

The 2020 census counted 31,753 residents, making Bangor the third most populous city in Maine behind Portland and Lewiston.

Does Bangor require registration of a vacant house?

Yes, in listed zoning districts. Registration is required within 60 days of the building becoming vacant, with exemptions for active-duty service members' residences and owners on extended absences who have a property manager. Fee deferrals are available in some cases.

Who pays the transfer tax when I sell in Bangor?

It is split evenly between seller and buyer. The rate is $2.20 for each $500 of value, and it is paid when the deed is recorded.

Is Bangor at risk of flooding?

Parts of the city have flooded from Penobscot River high water and ice jams, mostly in spring. Check FEMA's flood map for your address.

South Portland at a glance

South Portland is a Cumberland County city on Portland Harbor, directly across the water from Portland's skyline. It covers about 14 square miles, roughly 12 of them land, with Portland to the north, Cape Elizabeth and Scarborough to the south and Westbrook to the west. The July 2025 estimate is 27,007 residents.

The city is a patchwork of small named areas and not one center. They include Ferry Village, the oldest, along with Cushing's Point, Knightville, Mill Creek, Ligonia, Pleasantdale, Brick Hill, Redbank, Cash Corner, Thornton Heights, Meetinghouse Hill and Willard Beach. The Maine Mall district is its own part of town.

  • Ferry Village is the oldest neighborhood, so expect older construction there.
  • Willard Beach, a three-mile paved Greenbelt with harbor views and 40-acre Hinckley Park add to a buyer's interest in many areas.
  • The Maine Mall district and Mill Creek are commercial, so nearby homes sit close to retail traffic.

The main runway of the Portland International Jetport lies inside South Portland's limits, even though the terminal is in Portland. Homes under flight paths can draw questions about noise, so be ready with an honest answer.

How is property tax billed in South Portland?

The city sends one mailing a year with two payment stubs, due in May and November. Quarterly billing is gone. The City Council sets the exact rate and due dates each year in the budget orders, so confirm them with the Finance Department before you set a closing date.

The fiscal 2026 mil rate is $13.65 per $1,000 of assessed value, up 3.4 percent from $13.20 and about 30 percent below the 2019 rate of $19.70. Assessments are set as of April 1. The city reports a 100 percent certified ratio against a state minimum of 91 percent.

The city makes assessment adjustments in-house, and small adjustments are expected for fiscal 2027. If you think your value is wrong, call the assessing office.

What happens if South Portland property taxes are behind?

Back taxes here move along Maine's lien schedule, and selling can end the problem. The collector may mail a 30-day demand notice anywhere from 8 months to a year after commitment (36 M.R.S. section 942), then files a lien certificate. Leave the lien alone for 18 months and section 943 treats the lien mortgage as foreclosed.

  • The City Council can weigh hardship abatements for owners who cannot afford the tax.
  • To challenge an error or illegality, apply within 185 days of commitment under 36 M.R.S. section 841.

If you sell, the bill is paid out of closing proceeds. A written proration agreement with the buyer also lets the treasurer record a certificate showing you paid your share.

In practice, the order is simple. Call Finance at 207-767-7612 for the balance, give it to the title company, and have the payoff written into the closing statement. Homeowners who wait until the lien stage have fewer choices, because the clock to foreclosure is running by then.

Selling a house that needs work or has an unusual history

South Portland's older areas, and its wartime-era neighborhoods, include houses with additions, old wiring and aging roofs. A buyer who uses a mortgage will usually order an inspection and appraisal, and the lender may require repairs. A direct buyer who takes the house as-is removes that step.

Probate is another common reason to skip a listing. When an owner has died, the family often needs time, paperwork and a firm closing date, not repeated showings. Ask your attorney or the title company what the deed needs before anything is signed.

If the house sits near the flight path, the Maine Mall or Mill Creek, say so honestly. A buyer who learns about noise or traffic after an inspection may renegotiate, while a buyer told up front rarely does.

What to bring and what happens at closing

Closing in South Portland follows the same steps as anywhere in Maine. The title company confirms who owns the house and what liens are on it, prepares a settlement statement, and records the deed at the Cumberland County registry. Your mortgage payoff, any unpaid tax and your half of the transfer tax come out of the price.

  • Deed and a photo ID.
  • Latest mortgage statement, so the payoff can be calculated through the closing date.
  • Current tax bill and a balance from the Finance Department.
  • Rental registration and tenant details, if the building has three or more units or a short-term rental.
  • Homestead exemption information, since a new owner must apply on their own.

Because bills come twice a year, in May and November, the tax period is normally split between you and the buyer at closing. Ask for a draft settlement statement a few days ahead.

Transfer tax and closing costs

Maine's transfer tax is $2.20 per $500 of value, split evenly between buyer and seller. Transfers on or after November 1, 2025 also pay an extra $3.80 per $500 above $1 million.

The deed is recorded at the Cumberland County registry, and recording costs $40 for most submitters. Any exemption has to be stated on the declaration of value form. Maine Revenue Services publishes the transfer tax rules.

Rental rules for South Portland owners

Owners of buildings with three or more dwelling units or rooming units must register them with the city. That requirement comes from Chapter 5, Article VII of the South Portland Code of Ordinances, effective January 1, 2012. Short-term rentals must also be registered with the city.

When you sell a rental, tell buyers early whether it is registered, because the question comes up in every serious negotiation. A cash buyer can take over the building with tenants in place, so you need not empty it first.

How can I sell a South Portland house fast?

Cash closes fastest, while a listing may net more for a house in good shape. An updated house in a strong location can do well on the open market. One that needs a roof, a heating system or probate work often suits a direct buyer better.

  • Request a written offer from us and set it against a listing's net after commission and repairs.
  • Collect the deed, a mortgage statement and the latest tax bill.
  • Ask the Finance Department about any unpaid balance before closing.

We buy as-is and charge you no commission or closing fees. The offer is yours to decline.

Frequently asked questions

What is the South Portland mil rate?

The fiscal 2026 mil rate is $13.65 per $1,000 of assessed value. Ask the Finance Department for the current figure.

When are South Portland property taxes due?

Payments are due twice a year, in May and November, with one annual mailing that includes two stubs. The City Council sets the exact dates each year, so check the Finance Department page.

Does South Portland have a homestead exemption?

Yes. The Maine homestead exemption reduces taxable value by $25,000, which the city says is worth $341.25 in tax at the current rate.

Can I sell a South Portland house that is in a tax lien?

Yes. The lien payoff comes from your proceeds at closing. A lien that is not redeemed within 18 months of filing is deemed foreclosed under Maine law, so earlier action protects your equity.

Do South Portland short-term rentals need registration?

Yes. The city requires all short-term rentals to be registered. Buildings with three or more units must also be registered under the rental ordinance.

Sell My House Fast in Auburn, ME: Options, Costs and Cash Offers

Cash Home Buyers in Maine

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Auburn, ME sale

Sell Your Auburn House for Cash

Tell us about your Auburn house.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Auburn?
We buy Auburn houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Auburn at a glance

Auburn is the seat of Androscoggin County and sits on the Androscoggin River directly across from Lewiston. The two are called the Twin Cities, or Lewiston-Auburn, and share one metro area. About 24,000 people lived here at the 2020 census.

The city is big for its population, at 65.74 square miles, of which 59.33 are land. Over the years it took in land from Poland, Minot and the whole town of Danville, so a compact river downtown sits alongside farmland, lake property and rural roads. Lake Auburn supplies public water for the area.

That spread matters when you sell, because the rules change by neighborhood. A downtown house on public sewer faces one set of requirements, and a lake-area house on a septic system faces another, as the septic section below explains.

Much of the older housing dates from the shoe-factory boom, when the population grew from about 4,000 in 1860 to 12,000 by 1890. A house that old can have original wiring, an aging roof or a foundation that needs work. Those are the items a conventional buyer's inspector tends to list, and they are common reasons an owner looks for an as-is sale.

What does an Auburn property tax bill look like?

For the 2026-27 fiscal year, Auburn's rate is $24.50 per $1,000 of assessed value, and real estate bills are paid in two installments, one in September and one in March. The next installment is due March 15, 2027, with interest starting March 16.

Fiscal year 2026-27 tax figures
Tax detailFiscal year 2026-27
Tax rate$24.50 per $1,000 of assessment
State certified ratio73 percent
Second installment dueMarch 15, 2027 (interest begins March 16)
Homestead exemption$18,250 off assessment, worth $447.13 in tax

After a sale, send the bill on to your mortgage holder or to the new owner, and tell the tax office who now owns the house. Because the March installment falls in spring, a spring sale usually needs a payoff or a proration of that bill.

Exemptions and assessment appeals

Applications for the homestead, blind and veteran exemptions are due by April 1 for the following tax year. A buyer who wants the homestead exemption has to file their own application, since yours does not follow the house.

If you think your assessment is too high, Maine law requires a written request to the assessor within 185 days of the date the value was committed to the tax collector. The city explains the process on its abatements page. Auburn's assessing division also runs a citywide revaluation hub, so values may be reset in the coming years, and a buyer may ask what your new number will be.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Auburn house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Does Auburn require a septic inspection when you sell?

Yes, for homes in the Lake Auburn Watershed Overlay District that are not on public sewer. An inspection report has to be provided to the city when such a property is sold.

  • The rule covers owners in the Lake Auburn Watershed Overlay District whose buildings are not served by public sewer.
  • A certified subsurface wastewater system inspector must do the work, using minimum requirements set by the Maine Department of Health and Human Services.
  • The owner arranges and pays for the inspection, and costs vary by inspector.
  • Reports go to the city's Planning, Permitting and Code Department by email, paper or the SmartGov portal.
  • If the report shows a failed system, the local plumbing inspector reviews it, and a failed system has to be replaced with a new one.

The septic program began in spring 2025 under an ordinance effective July 15, 2024, and it cycles through five years of designated areas. A lake-area seller should check the city's map early, because a failed system turns a fast sale into a repair project.

A cash buyer who purchases as-is can take on that risk, but the inspection report still has to be filed. Ask any buyer, including us, how the septic requirement will be handled at the closing table.

Flood, watershed and vacant building rules

Two more city rules come up often: flood hazard permits and vacant building registration. The Planning, Permitting and Code Department administers both.

  • Flood hazard areas. FEMA's revised floodplain maps for Androscoggin County were adopted on July 8, 2013. Development in a special flood hazard area, including placing a manufactured home, needs a flood hazard development permit on top of any other permits. Check the FEMA map for your address before listing.
  • Taylor Pond and Lake Auburn overlays. Both watershed overlay districts carry extra zoning rules meant to protect water quality.
  • Vacant buildings. The owner of a vacant or abandoned building has to apply for a vacant building registration permit, and the permit is posted by the primary entrance. A fee schedule applies, with an added fee for buildings designated high impact. If you inherited an empty house, ask the code office whether it has to be registered.

None of these rules stops a sale. They do shape what a buyer's lender or inspector will ask for, which is why an as-is buyer can often close faster than a financed one.

Fees and taxes when you sell

As the seller you owe half of Maine's real estate transfer tax, plus any mortgage payoff, unpaid property tax and the cost of recording documents. The tax is $2.20 for every $500 of value, divided evenly between the two sides. Our Maine transfer tax guide covers the exemptions for inherited and divorce transfers.

Deeds in Auburn are recorded at the Androscoggin County Registry of Deeds, 2 Turner Street, Unit 4 (207-753-2500, extension 1981). The base fee is $35 by statute, and most Maine registries add a $5 surcharge. Our Maine deed recording guide has the details.

Property tax runs in two installments, so the current period is normally split between buyer and seller at closing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Auburn houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Should you list, sell yourself or take a cash offer?

Listing usually brings the widest pool of buyers and takes the longest. It also means preparing the house, since financed buyers usually order inspections. Selling it yourself saves the commission but puts the marketing, paperwork and negotiating on you. A cash offer is a purchase with no financing contingency, typically as-is, and the closing date is flexible.

We quote no price in advance and promise no amount. We look at the condition, location and what a house would sell for, and give you an offer you are free to turn down. Cash offers are often lower than a fully repaired retail listing, so compare the net you would receive, including repairs, carrying costs and commission, against the offer.

Cash offers fit best when the house needs work, when it was inherited, when tenants are in place, when a septic or title issue is pending, or when you need to close by a certain date.

Before you talk to any buyer, gather the deed, your mortgage payoff, the latest tax bill and, for a lake-area home, the status of your septic inspection.

Frequently asked questions

How do I sell my house fast in Auburn, ME?

The fastest route is usually a cash sale to a buyer who purchases as-is and does not need a mortgage. Listing with an agent is slower because buyers order inspections and appraisals. Either way, find out early whether your property needs a septic inspection report.

What is the property tax rate in Auburn, Maine?

For fiscal year 2026-27 the rate is $24.50 per $1,000 of assessed value. The second real estate installment is due March 15, 2027.

Do I need a septic inspection to sell in Auburn?

If the home is in the Lake Auburn Watershed Overlay District and is not served by public sewer, the city requires an inspection report when the property is sold. Homes on public sewer or outside the district are not covered by that rule.

Where are deeds recorded in Auburn?

At the Androscoggin County Registry of Deeds at 2 Turner Street, Unit 4, Auburn. Call 207-753-2500, extension 1981, to confirm fees and recording hours before you submit anything.

Can I sell an inherited house in Auburn?

Yes. Once the estate has the authority to sell, the house can be sold like any other. The deed that moves it from the estate to the heirs is exempt from transfer tax, but a later sale to a buyer is taxed, with the tax split evenly between buyer and seller.
